summary.headline: Adani Green H1 FY27 EBITDA from power supply rose 41% to INR7,957 crores at a 93% margin, with Khavda transmission delays cutting curtailment.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 power supply revenue rose 45% YoY to INR4,019 crores and EBITDA rose 51% to INR3,835 crores, a 92% margin. H1 energy sales grew 32% to 25.7 billion units, and operational capacity crossed 20 GW (20.8 GW portfolio). Management said Khavda evacuation (Phase 3) has slipped from end-FY27 Q3 to roughly the next quarter, which lowers the near-term 4.5-5 GW commissioning target. BESS commissioning (6.6 GWh installed, 3.5 GWh tied up) is being used to mitigate curtailment, and management reiterated the 10 GWh year-end target.

segments.name: Solar and wind power supply (operating portfolio)
segments.commentary: 20.8 GW operating; H1 solar CUF about 23% vs 24.8% in H1 FY26, attributed mainly to curtailment. Wind tied up at INR3.93/unit for 25 years.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: 3 GWh commissioned in Q2 at Khavda, taking installed storage to 6.6 GWh (over 50% of India's operational BESS). Target of 10 GWh by year-end, with management saying it expects to surpass this; 3.5 GWh tied up with AESL, 3.1 GWh still being contracted.

segments.name: Pumped storage
segments.commentary: 500 MW Chitravathi pumped storage project progressing towards completion by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Commissioning target for FY27 of 4.5-5 GW retained only if the Khavda Phase 3 evacuation corridor arrives by end of Q4 FY27; management said it now expects it next quarter (previously end of calendar 2026).
Battery storage: 10 GWh by end-FY27 reiterated, with management saying it expects to surpass it.
Capex programme of INR2.4 lakh crore through FY30 reiterated; management said no challenge foreseen in achieving it.

Leverage to stay in current range through FY28-FY29, then move towards 4.5x and below 4x as operating assets grow. Targeted build-out by FY29-FY30: about 45 GW RE, 5 GW pumped storage and 40-50 GWh batteries.
Management said second-half curtailment should be lower than first half because of accelerated BESS deployment.
capex_capacity: Operating capacity 20.8 GW; under-construction portfolio about 30% of total, with 5-7 GW of construction underway.
Khavda: 10.8 GWh of solar, wind and hybrid capacity commissioned; the 7 GW second corridor also reportedly delayed, with management focused on the first corridor.
Management said the 1 GW of BESS commissioned can absorb roughly 2-2.5 GW of solar (rule of thumb: divide by about 5), and BESS takes 8-10 months to build.
Balance-of-system and infrastructure at Khavda are being completed ahead of modules so that solar can be installed quickly once evacuation is available.
Management is also looking at other states including Rajasthan for additional capacity in case of Khavda delays.
demand_pricing: Q2 merchant (infirm) realisation about INR2.4/unit vs about INR2.1/unit last year; solar PPA with AESL is INR2.7/unit for 25 years.
Management attributed EBITDA growth mainly to better realisations, merchant prices, better wind speeds (lower rains), battery additions and cost efficiencies (O&M and employee costs flat).
All PPAs are take-or-pay; curtailment at the grid's request is paid as deemed generation where power was scheduled, per management.
Target returns of 13-14% ROA (EBITDA-based, per CFO), converting to a higher ROE on a 75:25 debt-equity structure.
Management said it prefers AA+ or higher counterparties on 25-year contracts; AESL is the current BESS and solar/wind counterparty.

qa_highlights.question: Is there acceleration in Khavda transmission, and what is the FY27 commissioning target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROW issues are slowing Power Grid and AESL. Target of 4.5-5 GW for FY27 is conditional on the corridor arriving by end of Q4 FY27; it was previously expected by end of calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to payments under curtailment for PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: All PPAs are take-or-pay; if the grid asks AGEL to back down on scheduled power, it is paid as deemed generation. Unscheduled power is not paid.

qa_highlights.question: How is interest cost moving with rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: About 72% of project loans are fixed for 3-5 years. AGE23L (about 15% of EBITDA) moved to AAA, with interest falling from 10-11% to 8.4%. Group cost of debt is 8.9%, vs 11.1% in 2019.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow faster than generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better realisations, merchant prices of INR2.4 vs INR2.1, better wind, BESS additions and cost efficiencies from digitisation and O&M.

qa_highlights.question: How much curtailment is embedded in the solar CUF decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the dip from 24.8% to 23% in H1 was mainly due to curtailment, with resource and plant operations better. It said 3-6 months of curtailment has little impact on 25-year asset returns.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage and capex plan change given BESS acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the capex plan is unchanged and BESS adds to it. Leverage stays in range through FY28-FY29, then falls towards 4.5x and below 4x after FY30.

risks_watch: Khavda Phase 3 evacuation corridor timing (now next quarter); a further slip would put the 4.5-5 GW FY27 commissioning target at risk.
Possible further delay on the second 7 GW Khavda corridor (Phase 6/7 scheme changes, possibly HVDC), which could affect the FY30 target.
BESS tie-up: 3.1 GWh of the 6.6 GWh installed capacity is still uncontracted; management has not disclosed counterparties.
Interest-rate exposure: about 30% of debt is USD, hedged for principal and interest (RG2 to FY30, RG1 to FY28, to be rolled over); rupee loans rely on fixed-rate terms.
Solar CUF decline due to curtailment, and whether H2 curtailment improves as management expects.
Leverage path: management guided it stays in range through FY28-FY29; watch FY28 net debt and EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Confident on financial performance and the capex programme, but guarded on transmission timing; management repeatedly described the Khavda Phase 3 delay as outside its control. Answers on C&I and BESS counterparty details were evasive, with management repeating its return and rating criteria rather than giving numbers.
key_quotes: Our operating and financial performance remained robust.
If curtailment would not have been there, this EBITDA would have been close to INR9,000 crores.
We remain committed to maintaining 13% to 14% ROE threshold by tying up capacities with AA+ counterparties.

growth.why: Management retained 4.5-5 GW FY27 commissioning only if Khavda Phase 3 evacuation arrives by Q4 FY27 (slipped from end-CY26), and reiterated BESS above 10 GWh by year-end with 6.6 GWh already installed; Q2 power supply revenue +45% YoY and EBITDA +51% YoY, though H1 solar CUF fell to ~23% from 24.8% on curtailment.
